title: Brasileirao standings double-count overlapping seasons across two CSVs
evidence: lib/brazilian_soccer_mcp/data.ex:7,11 map BOTH Brasileirao_Matches.csv (seasons 2012-2022, 380/yr) and novo_campeonato_brasileiro.csv (seasons 2003-2019, 380/yr) to competition "Brasileirao"; seasons 2012-2019 overlap. standings(2019) in query.ex:93-102 filters season=2019 & competition=Brasileirao, so it reduces 380+380=760 matches and normalize() (query.ex:3-13) merges the two files' team-name variants, counting each team's 38 games ~twice. _factual.json score=0.0: no 20-row 2019 table was obtainable.
suggestion: De-duplicate the two Brasileirao sources (pick one authoritative file per season, or dedup by season+teams+date) before computing standings.

title: normalize() collapses distinct clubs by stripping the state suffix
evidence: lib/brazilian_soccer_mcp/query.ex:11 strips a trailing "-XX" state code, so "Atletico-MG" and "Atletico-PR" both normalize to "atletico" and are merged in standings/team_stats; this plus cross-file name-format drift ("Athletico-PR" vs "Atletico-PR") yields the 34-row 2019 table seen in _factual.json instead of 20.
suggestion: Normalize for matching without discarding the state code that disambiguates same-named clubs.

title: MCP tool definitions expose empty inputSchema (no properties)
evidence: lib/brazilian_soccer_mcp/server.ex:67 every tool is inputSchema: %{type: "object"} with no properties/required, so an MCP client/LLM cannot discover argument names (team, season, competition, first_team, ...). The server, tools/list, tools/call and escript entrypoint DO exist (server.ex:8-69, lib/mix/tasks/mcp.ex, mix.exs escript), so R1 itself is satisfied; this is a usability/discoverability defect, not a missing requirement.
suggestion: Populate each tool's inputSchema with the named properties its handler reads in server.ex call/1.
